topic.title: Bionic skin with hair follicle regeneration capability from acoustic fluids-mediated 3D printing
topic.abstract: Tissue engineering holds substantial potential for constructing normal skin with appendages such as hair follicles, directly restoring skin's complete physiological functions. The current challenge lies in recreating biomimetic hair follicle organs with high-level cell density and architecture. Here, we developed an acoustofluidic-assisted 3D bioprinting platform to fabricate bionic skins with efficient hair follicle regeneration capability. Pre-formed hair follicle germs, derived from co-cultured epidermal and dermal mesenchymal stem cells, were encapsulated within a hydrogel bioink. Controlled acoustic fields generated flow vortices that directed cell migration and promoted organized cellular assembly from initially disordered states. Guided cell aggregates were then patterned through bioprinting to construct a grid-structured bionic skin. This architecture provided stable 3D support while maintaining high porosity, enabling efficient gas exchange. The printed bionic skin exhibited well-organized spatial cell distribution, high cellular viability, and promising differentiation potential. Further in vivo experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the bionic skin in accelerating mature hair regeneration, showing promise for clinical alopecia treatment.
